classification.difficultyReason: Recognise similar cones without a supplied similarity step, express the changing radius in terms of depth, and solve the resulting cubic volume relationship for the half-volume depth.

content.prompt:
The volume of ice-cream in the cone is half the volume of the cone.
The cone has a $3\text{ cm}$ radius and height of $14\text{ cm}$, as shown.
What is the depth of the ice-cream, correct to $2$ decimal places?

spec.description: Inverted cone with a solid top rim and silhouette, a centre dot, a red dashed radius, an internal dashed elliptical surface, full-height dimension and depth dimension from the surface to the apex. The ice-cream label is moved below the internal surface to agree with the depth arrow and supplied answer. No shading is retained.
spec.mathematics: Full cone radius 3 cm and height 14 cm. The unknown depth is measured from the apex to the internal horizontal surface. The smaller cone is similar to the full cone. Diagram proportions do not supply numerical measurements.
spec.answerVisibility: Only source givens and the unknown-depth relationship are visible; the calculated depth is absent.

answer.worked:
Let $d$ be the depth and $r$ the radius of the ice-cream surface. The smaller cone and full cone are similar.
$$\begin{align*}\frac{r}{3}&=\frac{d}{14}\\r&=\frac{3d}{14}\\\frac{1}{3}\pi\left(\frac{3d}{14}\right)^2d&=\frac{1}{2}\times\frac{1}{3}\pi(3)^2(14)\\\left(\frac{d}{14}\right)^3&=\frac{1}{2}\\d&=14\sqrt[3]{\frac{1}{2}}\\d&\approx11.11\text{ cm}\end{align*}$$
